sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and button styles
sections.what: Brings in the React library, the slot helper that lets a button act as another element, the variant helper, and the class joining helper. It defines the look of each button variant (default, destructive, outline, secondary, ghost, link) and each size (default, small, large, icon).
sections.why: One shared button keeps the whole app's buttons looking consistent.
sections.watch_out: Changing a variant style here changes every button of that kind across the whole app.

sections.name: ButtonProps
sections.title: Button component and its settings
sections.what: Defines the props a button accepts, including its variant, size, and whether it should pass its look to a child element. Renders a standard button element, or the child element when asked to. Passes through all normal button attributes, such as click handlers.
sections.why: Lets other files use one button component with a fixed look, while still accepting custom styling.
sections.watch_out: Passing asChild with an element that does not accept styling or a click handler will leave that element unstyled or inactive.

summary: The shared button used across the app, with options for color style, size, and borrowing the style for another element.
purpose: Keeps every button looking and behaving the same.
why: Likely reason: one shared button keeps the app consistent. The reason for the asChild option is not stated.
how: Defines named style choices (default, destructive, outline, secondary, ghost, link) and sizes. Combines them with any extra classes passed in. When asChild is on, it passes its style to the single element inside it instead of drawing its own button.
inputs: Variant, size, class name, asChild, and the usual button props.
outputs: A styled button, or a styled child element when asChild is on.
risks: Extra classes can override the variant's look. With asChild, the child element must accept the passed props, or clicks and styling may fail.
debug: If a button looks wrong, check its variant and size. If clicks fail when asChild is used, check that the child element accepts the props it receives.
